description:
Welcome to team Chronicles! We are a passionate development crew diving into the history of space exploration to build an immersive digital experience. Our focus is on combining robust full-stack web development with compelling UI/UX design to bring NASA's historic, discarded lunar and Martian hardware back to life.

We are currently looking for a creative UX/UI Designer to join our team and help us shape an intuitive, engaging interface targeted at inspiring the next generation of space explorers!
summary:
We developed an interactive, 3D planetary web application that serves as a digital museum for NASA's historic, discarded equipment resting on the Moon and Mars. Built using modern web technologies and 3D globe rendering, the platform allows users to explore interactive 3D surfaces, select specific landing coordinates, and uncover the stories behind iconic hardware like the Apollo descent stages, Viking landers, and the Opportunity rover.

Our solution directly addresses the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge by transforming static historical data into an engaging, visual storytelling experience. By including a dedicated "Junior Explorer Mode" alongside detailed technical profiles, the platform makes complex mission histories, scientific discoveries, and the current physical state of each relic accessible and exciting for school-age youth and general audiences alike.

This project is important because space exploration history is often locked away in dense technical archives. By bringing these silent pioneers back to life through interactive 3D exploration, we preserve the legacy of human ingenuity and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.
details:
Project Details: Space Relics

What it does and how it works

Space Relics is an interactive, 3D planetary web application that acts as a digital museum for NASA's historic, discarded equipment resting across the surfaces of the Moon and Mars. Built around a sleek, dark-themed space agency interface, the platform renders fully rotatable and zoomable 3D globes for both planetary bodies using CesiumJS. Users can toggle between the Moon and Mars, explore precise latitude and longitude coordinates, and click on glowing 3D markers anchored to iconic hardware (such as the Apollo 11 descent stage, Surveyor 3, the Opportunity rover, and the Viking 1 lander). Clicking any pin triggers a smooth camera fly-to animation and opens a slide-out story modal containing archival imagery, mission timelines, scientific breakthroughs, and the relic's current physical state. Furthermore, the platform features a dynamic dual-audience toggle allowing users to instantly switch between "Junior Explorer Mode" (simplified, engaging narratives tailored for school-age youth) and "Mission Analyst Mode" (detailed engineering and scientific data).

Benefits

  • Accessibility: Translates dense, technical NASA archives into an intuitive, visual, and highly engaging story that anyone can explore
  • Dual-Layer Engagement: Serves both casual learners/children through simplified storytelling and tech enthusiasts/students through deep-dive engineering metrics.
  • Zero-Latency Performance: Designed with a lightweight static architecture that loads instantly without lagging or depending on complex external server requests.

Intended Impact

The primary goal of Space Relics is to preserve the rich legacy of human space exploration and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space enthusiasts. By bringing silent pioneers left behind on alien worlds back into the public consciousness, the project fosters curiosity about planetary science and honors the historic missions that paved the way for modern space travel.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend Languages: HTML5 and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS (via CDN) for rapid, responsive, and modern dark-mode glassmorphism design.
  • 3D Globe & Spatial Engine: CesiumJS for high-performance 3D geospatial rendering, coordinate mapping, and camera animations.
  • Data Storage: A structured local relics.json dataset containing hardware coordinates, historical timelines, and dual-mode descriptions.
  • Development & Execution Environment: Visual Studio Code paired with the Live Server extension for local hosting and instant deployment.

Creativity

Unlike standard static galleries or dense text-heavy reports, Space Relics turns historical space data into an immersive exploration game. By merging 3D planetary GIS technology with dual-perspective storytelling (catering simultaneously to children and researchers), the application bridges the gap between hard science and creative education.

Factors Considered by the Team

  • 24-Hour Execution Window: We deliberately avoided heavy server-side backends or complex 3D modeling pipelines in favor of a robust JSON-driven frontend architecture to ensure a fully polished, bug-free deliverable within the strict hackathon timeline.
  • Target Audience Alignment: Careful attention was paid to the UI/UX design and narrative tone to ensure the content remains captivating, clear, and easy to digest for school-age youth.
  • Performance & Reliability: Utilizing lightweight CDNs and local JSON assets ensures the web app runs seamlessly across modern browsers without complex setup requirements.
